items.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen in GitHub Copilot
items.author: Allison
items.excerpt: Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Google’s latest Flash model, is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. It is designed for fast, efficient agentic coding, tool use, and multistep workflows, with improved instruction following over Gemini 3.8 Flash. This model is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing. See Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot for details. Availability in GitHub Copilot Gemini 4 Hydrogen is available to Copilot Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users. You can select the model in the model picker in: Visual Studio Code Visual Studio Copilot CLI GitHub Copilot coding agent GitHub Copilot app github.com GitHub Mobile on iOS and Android JetBrains IDEs Xcode Eclipse Copilot SDK Rollout will be gradual. Check back soon if you don’t see it yet. Enabling access Copilot Enterprise and Copilot Business plan administrators can manage access to Gemini 4 Hydrogen through the model policy in Copilot settings. Under default model enablement, new models are automatically enabled unless an administrator has turned off the global default or explicitly disables this model. Learn more To explore all models available in GitHub Copilot, see our documentation on models and get started with Copilot. Share your feedback Join the GitHub Community to share your feedback. The post Gemini 4 Hydrogen in GitHub Copilot appeared first on The GitHub Blog.

items.title: Manage AI Scan for repositories using the REST API
items.author: Allison
items.excerpt: You can now turn GitHub code scanning’s AI Scan for repositories on or off with the REST API at the organization and repository levels. This public preview adds a repository_scan setting to the existing AI Scan enablement endpoints. You can roll out AI Scan for repositories with scripts and infrastructure as code instead of changing settings one organization or repository at a time. Manage AI Scan for repositories at scale Set the repository_scan property to enabled or disabled on the AI Scan enablement endpoints: GET and PATCH /orgs/{org}/code-scanning/ai-scan GET and PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/ai-scan The setting works the same way as the existing pr_scan setting for AI Scan for pull requests: When an organization disables AI Scan for repositories, its repositories can’t enable it When an organization enables it, its repositories inherit the setting and can opt out individually When an enterprise policy doesn’t allow AI Scan, requests to enable it return a 422 error You can update pr_scan and repository_scan in the same request. If either change is blocked, the request returns a 422 error and neither setting changes. Turning on AI Scan for repositories doesn’t start a scan. Users with write access still run scans on demand, and each scan consumes GitHub Code Security AI credits. Who can use it Organization owners and security managers can manage the organization setting. Repository administrators can opt individual repositories out. AI Scan for repositories is available for public repositories owned by organizations and for private or internal repositories with GitHub Code Security or GitHub Advanced Security. Enterprise owners must first allow AI Scan in the enterprise policy. GitHub Enterprise Server isn’t supported. To get started, see REST API endpoints for code scanning and AI Scan for a repository’s backlog. Join the discussion in the GitHub Community. The post Manage AI Scan for repositories using the REST API appeared first on The GitHub Blo
items.why_it_matters: REST API control of GitHub AI Scan lets us roll out AI code scanning across client repos via scripts and IaC, useful for security baselines on GitHub-hosted projects.

Yesterday we covered reports that NVIDIA’s board was preparing to replace Jensen Huang following an NYT report of an affair with an accused Chinese spy. Following news of a second affair, today NVIDIA announced his resignation (correlation/causation is debatable here), presumably forced by the board: View post on X ↗ There is also some discussion of the extent that Chinese models can demonstrably be shown to be trained on Blackwell GPUs that they should not have access to… though the scale is debated. After 33 years, Jensen Huang has stepped down as CEO, president and boardmember. Colette Kress, NVIDIA’s CFO since 2013, will keep that job while serving as interim CEO… leading into what will presumably the best attended earnings call in the history of $NVDA next week. AI News for 11/11/2026-11/12/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews' website lets you search all past issues. items.title: AI Ambition: ArtCraft Cloned Photoshop and Now Wants to "Rebuild Everything"
items.author: Richard MacManus
items.excerpt: The theme of day two of the AI Engineer Code Summit in San Francisco was increasing ambition using AI. And there have been few projects as ambitious as ArtCraft in the AI era. So far the fledgling company has released 17 open source versions of popular software tools, starting with a Photoshop alternative built from scratch in Rust called PhotoCraft. You could feel the excitement in the room this morning when ArtCraft founder and CEO Brandon Thomas presented a kind of manifesto for AI-based open source at AIE Code. When he mentioned that ArtCraft had cloned Adobe’s Acrobat, with a product called PdfCraft, it got a round of applause from the audience. In wrapping up, his rallying cries of “let's take back the entire internet” and “let's rebuild everything” were greeted with whoops and cheers. Thomas began his presentation by reliving the internet’s early history. In his view, the web started out with the right intentions, but things got screwed up once Web 2.0 hit the mainstream. “We had a bunch of chat applications that were completely open,” he said, regarding the 1990s internet. “So, IRC is like Discord, but you can spin up your own servers that you actually own. You can use whatever programs to automate them and interrogate them without rules.” His point wasn’t necessarily that everything was open source, but that web users could freely build things. With Flash, for example — a commercial animation tool eventually acquired by Adobe — “kids were making all kinds of animations.” When Web 2.0 came along, with its superior broadband and smartphones, “it brought everybody into the fold.” Thomas acknowledged that this widened the scope of internet software, but at the cost of that freedom to build with leading apps. “The diffuse, experimental, early web started to disappear,” he said. “The APIs got taken away from us, and then we started seeing distribution being gatekept by the big providers.” It seems Adobe in particular annoyed Thomas. items.title: llm-gemini 0.37
items.excerpt: Release: llm-gemini 0.37 Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen today - the lowest cost member of the Gemini 4 family. It's actually not too far off the price of its much bigger siblings, Carbon and Argon. I'm finding Gemini 4's pricing really confusing. Here's the pricing scheme: Model Dates Input ($/M) Cached input Output Gemini 4 Carbon Through Nov 30, 2026 $2.00 $0.10 $10.00 From Dec 1, 2026 $4.00 $0.20 $20.00 Gemini 4 Argon Through Nov 30, 2026 $2.00 $0.10 $10.00 From Dec 1, 2026 $4.00 $0.20 $20.00 Gemini 4 Hydrogen $1.50 $0.075 $7.50 Carbon and Argon are the same price, and both are scheduled to double in price on December 1st. If they're the same price, why have two different models? Google says that Argon "delivers Gemini 4 intelligence with faster responses and lower token spend per turn compared to Gemini 4 Carbon" - so it may be priced the same, but it will use less tokens per task. Hydrogen, supposedly the cheap model, is currently only a 25% discount on its more capable peers. The Hydrogen price will make more sense after December 1st, when it will represent a 75% discount. It's still considerably more expensive than Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna - they're both $0.10/$0.50, so Hydrogen is 15x that. I had Hydrogen generate some pelicans. Here's a full comparison grid showing the pelicans for all three members of the Gemini 4 family at their three supported effort levels: Considering how close they are in price, the difference in pelican quality for Hydrogen is quite stark. Here's how Google describe Hydrogen's intended position in their mix of models: In real-world software development, while teams rely on frontier models like Carbon and Argon for deep architectural judgment when designing systems or untangling subtle bugs, they still need a fast, disciplined execution model for writing code, running tests, and verifying changes. Hydrogen is built to stand on its own as a model for everyday work — or to pair with Carbon and Argon as the high-efficiency exec
items.why_it_matters: Gives pricing detail for Gemini 4 Hydrogen and notes Carbon and Argon prices double on Dec 1, which affects cost planning for client Gemini integrations.

items.title: The Take-Home Test That Runs on Your Work Laptop: Inside the AccuraSoftHire Fake Interview Campaign
items.excerpt: Binance says its $6.34 billion theft began when an engineer ran a fake interview assignment on his work computer. JFrog has now exposed a fake company, AccuraSoftHire, built to run the same trick. We decoded the attacker's server history from a public Ethereum wallet and found npm packages from the interview task that stayed installable for up to seven months. Here is what to check on your developer machines.
items.why_it_matters: Fake interview campaign delivers malicious npm packages to developer machines and is tied to a $6.34B theft. A direct supply-chain risk for Node engineers and for hiring practices.

items.title: ARTEX: Attackers Adopted This AI Pentesting Tool in Three Months. Leaked Secrets Are Its Fastest Way In.
items.excerpt: ARTEX is an open-source tool where AI agents run a penetration test on their own. Since August 2026, state-aligned groups, criminal crews and one runaway research agent have pointed ARTEX at hundreds of organizations. In one case, an agent went from a GitHub search for leaked secrets to stolen cloud data in five minutes. This post covers what ARTEX is, who uses ARTEX, how to spot ARTEX activity, and how you remove its easiest way in.
items.why_it_matters: Autonomous AI pentesting agents exploiting leaked secrets from GitHub within minutes is a direct threat to our and clients' repos and cloud accounts; worth reviewing secret-scanning and rotation practices.
